newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee barely changed by close despite NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee barely changed by close despite NY.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures were barely changed by the close after fluctuating in a modest range despite firmer New York values.
Traders said dealings were slow and centred on the Jan/March switch which narrowed slightly to $52 from $57 on Thursday.
By the finish, March firmed $3 at $1,278 a tonne while January was $2 down at $1,330.
Traders said there was a dearth of industry or fund interest ahead of the long Christmas holidays.
News Brazil agreed to call for a producer meeting to consider further cuts in first half 1997 exports came as a surprise to some traders.
The news camea after Brazilian officials met with an African coffee delegation, which was pushing for the idea of further cutting producer exports in the first half of 1997.
"The Brazilians said yesterday they were not interested. I think it's (the plan) a dead duck basically," said one.
The delegation, led by Ivory Coast, earlier visited Colombia where both sides agreed on the need to cut exports by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries by 2.5 million 60-kg bags.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) 1996/97 coffee crop report due later tonight is not expected to yield any surprises but traders said it would still come under their scrutiny.
In London, traders said funds were unlikely to resume short-covering buying unless prices rise to above $1,300 basis second-month March.
Roasters are either well-covered or holding back their purchases until after the New Year.
